text.text_excerpt: I've only been to the rooftop bar. The views are amazing. It's a really old hotel in the Garden District that has been kept nicely. This place is absolutely charming. There is usually a short wait to get on the elevator to get to the roof. The place gets crowded, but it's worth it for the drinks, random conversations and the city views. The crowd is usually a mixture of locals and tourists. This is a great place to go after work or dinner.

How do you describe perfection? I have no idea, but I am sure going to try. As soon as I heard the Pontchartrain Hotel was reopening I was all about it. I was all about the rooms. I was all about the Bayou Bar. I was all about the Silver Whistle. The hotel itself is heaven. It feels like an old style hotel and when you check in at the counter, you can just tell you are in for something special. One of the things I really like is that you get keys to the rooms. REAL KEYS and not cards! I hate the cards and this "old school" touch made me so happy. The room itself is lovely. The room I was in cost $100 for a night and it was gorgeous. The bed was huge and comfy, there was an honor bar, ther...

This place is great, semi grand, and beautiful. Reminds me of the old south. I can see the historical slave servants serving in the breakfast room. I can't get that out of my head because of how the place looks. This angers me. But, the hotel does not reflect that past in its service, attention to detail, kindness and cleanliness. But seriously you should have full kitchens and/ or dishwashers. Kitchenettes are always half way there. Odd review I know. Oh by the by they have ghost or so some of the other guest have told me. So far no experiences myself.
